met_analysis:
The Low-Pressure Area (Remnant of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”) over southeast Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood persisted over the same region at 1430 hrs IST of 31st October, 2026. However, the associated cyclonic circulation now extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level as the system is under the influence of extra tropical westerlies.
The Well Marked Low pressure area over Southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining areas of Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea moved west-northwestwards and concentrated into a depression at 1130 hrs IST of today, the 31st October 2026 over the same region near latitude 10.0N and 90.2E, about 330 km west-southwest of Sri Vijayapuram, 300 km west-northwest of Car Nicobar, 1140 km east-southeast of Chennai and 1200 km southeast of Machilipatnam. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a deep depression over Southeast Bay of Bengal during next 12 hours. Continuing to move west- northwestwards, it is very likely to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over Southeast & adjoining areas of Southwest & West-central Bay of Bengal during subsequent 12 hours and reach over Westcentral Bay of Bengal near Andhra Pradesh coast around evening of 2nd November 2026.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood at 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The fresh Western Disturbance as a trough in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 65°E to the north of Lat. 29°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Maharashtra coast & neighbourhoodbetween 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from Southeast Arabian sea off Kerala-Karnataka coast to the upper air cyclonic circulation over south Maharashtra coast & neighbourhoodat 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
